It spawns the Vite preview node process itself, detached, and stop() signals the whole process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 3s) and awaits the child's 'exit'. verify() and inspect() call preview.stop() in a finally block that every exit path passes through. criteria.rationale: Bounded wait: the inspect scripts have no readiness code of their own. Both copies of inspect-presentation.mjs import `startPreview` (with `run` and `freePort`) from './verify.mjs' at line 9, so they use the same `startPreview` defined in each verify.mjs at lines 118-163. That function's only readiness wait is `for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++)`, which probes `fetch(previewUrl(port))` with a 200 ms delay between attempts. It breaks out early when the child has exited (`if (dead) break`). Once the attempts run out it awaits stop() and throws 'preview did not become ready'. The wait is therefore capped and fails rather than hanging. Build before preview: verify() awaits `run('npm',['run','build'],root)` at line 235, and `run` resolves only on the child's 'close' event (lines 96-105). It returns a build failure on a non-zero code before reaching startPreview at line 264. inspect() awaits the same `run` for the build at lines 236-238 and throws on failure before calling startPreview at line 242. Ready-URL parsing: readiness is an HTTP probe; stdout is only collected into `output` for the error message. Nothing parses a printed ready URL, so the ANSI and chunk clause does not apply. Judge C says each awaited fetch lacks its own timeout. The clause asks that the readiness wait is bounded, and the cited loop bounds it with an attempt cap, a delay, a dead-child exit and a final throw. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited with a polling `page.waitForFunction` on data-step-index (verify.mjs:209-213, inspect-presentation.mjs:202-206). The verify() finally block awaits `browser.close()` and `preview.stop()` (verify.mjs:282-285). stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child's 'exit' (verify.mjs:131-147). main() calls process.exit only after verify() resolves (verify.mjs:297-304). votes.rationale: The Talk hands its steps and title to the kit's Presentation instead of reimplementing navigation, stage or chrome. The shared Scene builds its diagram only from kit primitives (SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Label, Emphasis, Frame). Each step is a kit Step carrying Scene, payload and groupKey. The demo has no motion, layout or navigation logic of its own.
evidence: Talk.tsx renders <Presentation className="how-to" steps={STEPS} title="How to Use This Skill to Make a Presentation" initialMode="browse" />, imported from present…
scene.tsx HowToScene wraps its output in <SceneLayer> and <Appear key={id}>, and NODES builds every entity from kit Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Label, Emphasis and Frame.
steps.ts types the steps as Step<ScenePayload> with Scene: HowToScene, payload: { index } and groupKey: 'how-to'.
Presentation.tsx wires usePresentationNav, Header, Toc, Stage, Footer and Attribution, and passes through canvas, brand and attribution.

votes.rationale: The Talk hands its steps and title to the kit's Presentation and builds the scene from kit primitives. It does not re-implement navigation, stage mounting, layout morphing or presence handling. votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of the port, either an ephemeral port that freePort() reserved, closed and then reused, or a user-supplied --port. The only ownership check is `if (dead) break` at the top of each loop iteration, which samples the child's liveness before each request. Readiness is not taken from the child's own announcement. The child's exit is not raced against the probe. A stale server already listening on the port can answer the fetch before the child's exit is observed. --strictPort alone is insufficient under the guidance.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs startPreview loop: `for (...) { if (dead) break; try { const res = await fetch(previewUrl(port)); if (res.ok) return { stop } } ... }`
`dead` is set only by `exited.then(() => (dead = true))` and is read once per iteration before the fetch; stdout is never parsed for readiness
freePort() closes its server before the preview binds, so the port is not held; `port ?? (await freePort())` also accepts a reused port

votes.rationale: All nine public primitives exported from the kit index (Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Arrow, Appear, SceneLayer, plus Presentation) use typed props, not an untyped bag. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip all go through BaseNode. Its props extend DomPassthrough, which is HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> minus the props that conflict with motion. BaseNode spreads `...rest` first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity, so callers cannot override the identity hooks. It destructures the kit-only props (as, kind, id, x, y, w, h) so they never reach the DOM, and Box removes `Icon` the same way. Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are thin wrappers that pass a fixed `kind` and `as` to BaseNode, and their prop types are BaseNodeProps. Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer type their props with explicit interfaces plus DataAttrs, which allows only `data-*` attributes. Each spreads `...rest` first and then applies its data-presentation-* hooks. Arrow also sets data-presentation-entity={id} after the spread. It destructures from, to, bend, bidirectional, headSize and id, so none reach the DOM. Appear destructures `delay` and SceneLayer takes no kit-only props, so neither forwards a kit-only prop to the DOM.

votes.rationale: All three clauses hold for every public primitive that SKILL.md lists: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. (1) Typing: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are all built on BaseNodeProps. That type extends NodeProps, Placement and DomPassthrough, and DomPassthrough is Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, ...>, so these are typed as the rendered element's props, not a Record<string, unknown> bag. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are plain type aliases of BaseNodeProps. Box extends it with only Icon. Appear, SceneLayer and Arrow use explicit interfaces that add the template literal type DataAttrs for data-* attributes. Those interfaces are narrow and typed, not an untyped bag. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props. BaseNode spreads {...rest} first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Appear spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-scene-layer. Arrow spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-node="arrow" and data-presentation-entity, and its path hooks are fixed. A caller cannot override any of these. Frame, Emphasis, Label and SymbolChip pass {...props} before nothing of their own except as/kind, and BaseNode applies the identity attributes last. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w, h and style, and Box destructures Icon, so none of them reach the DOM element. Appear destructures delay and Arrow destructures from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize. The repo copy src/presentation-kit/nodes/BaseNode.tsx is identical to the bootstrap copy.

result.rationale: Which tests drive a browser: vitest.config.ts runs tests/unit in jsdom. Those unit tests drive no browser; captureSteps there gets a stub page whose waitForTimeout only logs (inspect-lib.test.ts:129-159). The e2e and integration configs include only tests/e2e and tests/integration, which are the four browser test files: e2e-001, e2e-002, int-001 and int-002. All four are quoted in full. None of them calls waitForTimeout, a setTimeout-based sleep or any other fixed delay. The only setTimeout is in e2e-002 line 92, inside a string written into the fixture's scene to inject a page fault; it is not a test wait. Each test starts verify or inspect through workspace `run`, which resolves on the child's 'close' event (workspace.ts:27-37). The tests then assert on the exit code, output and report.json once the process has ended. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited with a polling `page.waitForFunction` on data-step-index (verify.mjs:209-213, inspect-presentation.mjs:202-206). The isListening and pgrep checks after exit (e2e-001:46-50, e2e-002:28-35) read settled state, not an immediate read standing in for a wait. The verify() finally block awaits `browser.close()` and `preview.stop()` (verify.mjs:282-285). stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child's 'exit' (verify.mjs:131-147). main() calls process.exit only after verify() resolves (verify.mjs:297-304). So by the time `run` resolves, cleanup has finished. Judge C cites the scripts' SETTLE_MS and settleMs delays. Those are capture-timing features of the scripts under test, and each runs only after the step index has been awaited by polling. They are not test waits for a transition. Int-002's 'waits for the settle interval' test reads a waitedMs value recorded in a finished report; it does not sleep. C's reason therefore does not show any browser test sleeping instead of waiting for state. Judges A and B ruled pass for the same reasons shown here.

checks.rationale: The criterion defines coverage this way: "a behavior is covered when a recorded observation shows its scenario's user-visible outcome." Saying a scenario was exercised is not enough. The round-0 log for evolving-scene-presentations has one general sentence: "DOM values, interactive controls, and screenshots were inspected." After that it only lists scenarios as "Exercised". Several significant interaction behaviors have no recorded observation of their outcome anywhere in the packet: - Present mode is title-focused: nothing shows that only the marker and title appear while the caption, table of contents and prev/next are hidden. - Mode toggle preserves position: nothing shows the step index staying the same across a toggle. - Touch swipe: no swipe action or result is recorded. - Direct jump: no jump action or result is recorded. - Controls keep their keys: no test of a focused control is recorded. The records offer only partial support: - The handoff's note that "Present mode toggles with `P`" names the key binding. It does not show title-focused content or preserved position. - The screenshot index shows Previous disabled on the first step and Next disabled on the last. That covers clamping only in part. - The round-1 ArrowRight advance happened in the bootstrap fixture. It does not cover the sample's modes, swipe or jump. The record never discloses these behaviors as unexercised or blocked by the environment. It claims they were exercised. Because coverage requires a recorded outcome, they count as omissions without disclosure, and the environmental exemption the majority relies on applies only to the prompt/dialogue scenarios. The decider says per-claim proof belongs under usable proof. That does not hold here, because this criterion's own coverage definition requires a recorded outcome observation. Present mode, the mode toggle and touch swipe are each significant user-visible behaviors that the environment allowed. Under the fail clause, one such behavior omitted without disclosure is enough to fail.

verification-tooling.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of a port. That port is either one freePort() reserved, closed, then reused, or a user-supplied --port. The only ownership check is `if (dead) break` at the top of each loop iteration, which samples child liveness before each request. Child exit is not raced against the probe, and readiness is not taken from the child's own announcement. A stale server on that port can answer the fetch first. The guidance names this pattern as a fail, and --strictPort alone is insufficient.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs startPreview: `for (...) { if (dead) break; try { const res = await fetch(previewUrl(port)); if (res.ok) return { stop } } ... }`

engineering-quality.rationale: All three clauses are met by the node primitives in the packet. (1) Typed props: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use BaseNodeProps, which extends NodeProps, Placement and DomPassthrough. DomPassthrough is HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> minus a few conflicting keys. Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use explicit interfaces plus DataAttrs, a `data-${string}` mapped type. None uses Record<string, unknown> or a similar untyped bag. (2) Identity hooks after caller props: BaseNode spreads `{...rest}` first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Arrow spreads `{...rest}` before data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Appear and SceneLayer spread `{...rest}` before their data-presentation-* hooks. The wrappers pass `kind` and `as` before `{...props}`, but BaseNodeProps has no `kind` or `as` key, so a caller cannot override them under the types, and BaseNode applies the data hooks after the spread anyway. (3) Kit-only props kept off the DOM: BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w and h. Box destructures Icon. Arrow destructures id, from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize. Appear destructures delay. Presentation.tsx is not in the packet. It is the root shell, not a node primitive, so I did not weigh it.

votes.rationale: All nine public primitives exported from the kit index (Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Arrow, Appear, SceneLayer, plus Presentation) use typed props, not an untyped bag. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip all go through BaseNode. Its props extend DomPassthrough, which is HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> minus the props that conflict with motion. BaseNode spreads `...rest` first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity, so callers cannot override the identity hooks. It destructures the kit-only props (as, kind, id, x, y, w, h) so they never reach the DOM, and Box removes `Icon` the same way. Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are thin wrappers that pass a fixed `kind` and `as` to BaseNode, and their prop types are BaseNodeProps. Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer type their props with explicit interfaces plus DataAttrs, which allows only `data-*` attributes. Each spreads `...rest` first and then applies its data-presentation-* hooks. Arrow also sets data-presentation-entity={id} after the spread. It destructures from, to, bend, bidirectional, headSize and id, so none reach the DOM. Appear destructures `delay` and SceneLayer takes no kit-only props, so neither forwards a kit-only prop to the DOM.

votes.rationale: All three clauses hold for every public primitive that SKILL.md lists: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. (1) Typing: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are all built on BaseNodeProps. That type extends NodeProps, Placement and DomPassthrough, and DomPassthrough is Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, ...>, so these are typed as the rendered element's props, not a Record<string, unknown> bag. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are plain type aliases of BaseNodeProps. Box extends it with only Icon. Appear, SceneLayer and Arrow use explicit interfaces that add the template literal type DataAttrs for data-* attributes. Those interfaces are narrow and typed, not an untyped bag. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props. BaseNode spreads {...rest} first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Appear spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-scene-layer. Arrow spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-node="arrow" and data-presentation-entity, and its path hooks are fixed. A caller cannot override any of these. Frame, Emphasis, Label and SymbolChip pass {...props} before nothing of their own except as/kind, and BaseNode applies the identity attributes last. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w, h and style, and Box destructures Icon, so none of them reach the DOM element. Appear destructures delay and Arrow destructures from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize. The repo copy src/presentation-kit/nodes/BaseNode.tsx is identical to the bootstrap copy.

first_results.rationale: All three clauses are met in both repository copies and both bootstrap copies. (1) Bounded readiness: startPreview waits in a loop capped at 100 iterations with a 200 ms delay between probes. It breaks early if the child process has exited, and when it gives up it stops the preview and throws 'preview did not become ready'. The browser-side waits are also bounded: waitForSelector('[data-step-count]', { timeout: 10000 }), and the step waitForFunction uses a 3000 ms or 5000 ms timeout. (2) Build before preview: verify() awaits run('npm', ['run','build']), which resolves only on the child's 'close' event, and returns a failure on a non-zero code before it calls startPreview. inspect() does the same whenever build is enabled. (3) Readiness does not parse the server's printed ready URL; it probes over HTTP with fetch. The ANSI/chunk clause therefore does not apply. Judge C's reason: an individual fetch carries no explicit AbortSignal. That does not decide the criterion. The readiness wait itself is capped by the loop bound and ends when the child dies. The guidance names no scenario in which a server accepts a connection and never answers, and the candidate produces no such server. Failing on that would mean failing on a hypothetical input. Judges A and B correctly found every clause met.

first_results.rationale: All three clauses hold for every primitive exported from src/presentation-kit/index.ts. (1) Typing: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use BaseNodeProps, which extends DomPassthrough, an Omit of HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>. These are the rendered element's props. Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use explicit, narrowly typed interfaces plus DataAttrs, a template-literal `data-${string}` map to string | number | boolean. None of the primitives uses an untyped Record<string, unknown> bag, and that bag is the failure the guidance names. Presentation uses a typed PresentationProps interface. (2) Identity hooks are applied after caller props. BaseNode spreads {...rest} and only then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Arrow spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-node='arrow' and data-presentation-entity={id}. Appear and SceneLayer spread {...rest} before data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-scene-layer. (3) Kit-only props are kept off the DOM. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w and h, and Box destructures Icon. Arrow destructures from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize, and Appear destructures delay. Judge C's reason: Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer declare custom interfaces rather than full SVG or div props. That does not decide the requirement. Those interfaces are typed rather than an untyped bag, and their passthrough is limited to typed data-* attributes, so the guidance's failure condition is not triggered.

first_results.rationale: The browser-backed tests are e2e-001, e2e-002, int-001 and int-002. They run verify or inspect as a subprocess through workspace.run(), which resolves only on the child's 'close' event. They then assert on the exit code, the output and the post-exit process state. None of the test files contains waitForTimeout, setTimeout or another sleep used as a wait. The single setTimeout in e2e-002 sits inside an injected page-code string that raises a fault; it is not a test wait. The isListening and pgrep checks run after verify has exited, and verify's stop() awaits the preview's exit before the process ends. So these checks read settled state; they are not immediate reads standing in for a wait. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited with waitForFunction on data-step-index. Judge C's reason: verify and inspect contain fixed settle delays (SETTLE_MS, settleMs). Those delays belong to the scripts under test, not to the tests, so they do not decide this criterion. int-002's waitedMs assertion checks the script's documented settle option and does not make the test itself sleep.

results.rationale: Bounded wait: the inspect scripts have no readiness code of their own. Both copies of inspect-presentation.mjs import `startPreview` (with `run` and `freePort`) from './verify.mjs' at line 9, so they use the same `startPreview` defined in each verify.mjs at lines 118-163. That function's only readiness wait is `for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++)`, which probes `fetch(previewUrl(port))` with a 200 ms delay between attempts. It breaks out early when the child has exited (`if (dead) break`). Once the attempts run out it awaits stop() and throws 'preview did not become ready'. The wait is therefore capped and fails rather than hanging. Build before preview: verify() awaits `run('npm',['run','build'],root)` at line 235, and `run` resolves only on the child's 'close' event (lines 96-105). It returns a build failure on a non-zero code before reaching startPreview at line 264. inspect() awaits the same `run` for the build at lines 236-238 and throws on failure before calling startPreview at line 242. results.rationale: All three clauses hold for every primitive exported from src/presentation-kit/index.ts. (1) Typing: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use BaseNodeProps, which extends DomPassthrough, an Omit of HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>. These are the rendered element's props. None of the primitives uses an untyped Record<string, unknown> bag, and that bag is the failure the guidance names. Presentation uses a typed PresentationProps interface. Appear and SceneLayer spread {...rest} before data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-scene-layer. (3) Kit-only props are kept off the DOM. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w and h, and Box destructures Icon. Arrow destructures from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize, and Appear destructures delay. results.rationale: Which tests drive a browser: vitest.config.ts runs tests/unit in jsdom. Those unit tests drive no browser; captureSteps there gets a stub page whose waitForTimeout only logs (inspect-lib.test.ts:129-159). The e2e and integration configs include only tests/e2e and tests/integration, which are the four browser test files: e2e-001, e2e-002, int-001 and int-002. All four are quoted in full. None of them calls waitForTimeout, a setTimeout-based sleep or any other fixed delay. The only setTimeout is in e2e-002 line 92, inside a string written into the fixture's scene to inject a page fault; it is not a test wait. Each test starts verify or inspect through workspace `run`, which resolves on the child's 'close' event (workspace.ts:27-37). The tests then assert on the exit code, output and report.json once the process has ended. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited with a polling `page.waitForFunction` on data-step-index (verify.mjs:209-213, inspect-presentation.mjs:202-206). The isListening and pgrep checks after exit (e2e-001:46-50, e2e-002:28-35) read settled state, not an immediate read standing in for a wait. The verify() finally block awaits `browser.close()` and `preview.stop()` (verify.mjs:282-285). stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child's 'exit' (verify.mjs:131-147). main() calls process.exit only after verify() resolves (verify.mjs:297-304). So by the time `run` resolves, cleanup has finished. Judge C cites the scripts' SETTLE_MS and settleMs delays. Those are capture-timing features of the scripts under test, and each runs only after the step index has been awaited by polling. They are not test waits for a transition. Int-002's 'waits for the settle interval' test reads a waitedMs value recorded in a finished report; it does not sleep. C's reason therefore does not show any browser test sleeping instead of waiting for state. Judges A and B ruled pass for the same reasons shown here.

audit_results.rationale: The criterion requires every readiness wait in both the verify and the inspect scripts to have a timeout, with build completing before the preview starts. In both verify.mjs copies, the startPreview defined there is a bounded loop: 100 iterations with a 200 ms delay, breaking out if the child dies and then stopping the preview and throwing. Verify also awaits `npm run build` to completion, and returns a failure on a non-zero code, before it calls startPreview. Readiness uses an HTTP probe, not printed-URL parsing, so the ANSI/chunk clause does not apply. In inspect-presentation.mjs, however, only lines 197-242 are quoted. Those lines call startPreview(root, previewPort), run and freePort, but the definitions or imports of these functions (lines 1-196) are never quoted. Nothing establishes that the inspect scripts' startPreview is the bounded loop from verify.mjs rather than a separate function with its own wait. Treating it as the same function would be inferring behaviour from a name. The build-before-preview ordering in inspect is shown, but the bounded-readiness clause for the inspect copies is not established by the quoted lines.

audit_results.rationale: All three clauses are met by the quoted material. (1) Bounded readiness: both inspect copies import startPreview from './verify.mjs' (line 9), and the quoted inspect() (231-273) has no readiness wait of its own. Its only preview start is startPreview at line 242. In both verify copies, startPreview's only readiness wait is a loop capped at 100 attempts with a 200 ms delay between them (148-160). It exits early if the child dies and then runs `await stop()` and throws 'preview did not become ready' (161-162), so the wait is bounded and fails rather than hanging. Each fetch has no timeout of its own, but the requirement asks only that the readiness wait has a timeout, and the attempt cap provides one. A server that hangs mid-request is a hypothetical the guidance does not name. (2) Build before preview: verify() awaits run('npm',['run','build']) at 235 and returns a failure on a non-zero code at 236. run resolves only on 'close' (96-105). startPreview comes later, at 264. inspect() awaits the same build at 236-238 and throws on failure before startPreview at 242. This holds identically in the repository copies and the template copies. (3) Ready-URL parsing: readiness is an HTTP probe, and stdout/stderr are only collected into `output` for the error message. Nothing parses a printed ready URL, so per the guidance the ANSI/chunk clause does not apply.

The e2e and integration configs include only tests/e2e and tests/integration, which are the four browser test files: e2e-001, e2e-002, int-001 and int-002. All four are quoted in full. None of them calls waitForTimeout, a setTimeout-based sleep or any other fixed delay. The only setTimeout is in e2e-002 line 92, inside a string written into the fixture's scene to inject a page fault; it is not a test wait. Each test starts verify or inspect through workspace `run`, which resolves on the child's 'close' event (workspace.ts:27-37). The tests then assert on the exit code, output and report.json once the process has ended. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited with a polling `page.waitForFunction` on data-step-index (verify.mjs:209-213, inspect-presentation.mjs:202-206). The isListening and pgrep checks after exit (e2e-001:46-50, e2e-002:28-35) read settled state, not an immediate read standing in for a wait. The verify() finally block awaits `browser.close()` and `preview.stop()` (verify.mjs:282-285). stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child's 'exit' (verify.mjs:131-147). main() calls process.exit only after verify() resolves (verify.mjs:297-304). So by the time `run` resolves, cleanup has finished. Judge C cites the scripts' SETTLE_MS and settleMs delays. Those are capture-timing features of the scripts under test, and each runs only after the step index has been awaited by polling. They are not test waits for a transition. Int-002's 'waits for the settle interval' test reads a waitedMs value recorded in a finished report; it does not sleep. C's reason therefore does not show any browser test sleeping instead of waiting for state. Judges A and B ruled pass for the same reasons shown here.

lines.text: All 27 listed scenarios were exercised at least once except where noted. The committed sample ran in Chromium through AXI at `127.0.0.1:5173/how-to-make-a-presentation`; DOM values, interactive controls, and screenshots were inspected. Helper captures cover all 9 steps at wide size and all 9 at narrow size, each with 0 warnings. Grouped-scene persistence/movement, delayed entry, departure, and continuing entity behavior were observed in the `group-probe` fixture. An ordinary distinct-Scene stable Arrow probe exposed F-001.

- **Exercised:** Step carries narration and identity; Order-derived numbering; Typed payloads reach presentation boundary; Persisting entity morphs; New entity enters after others settle; Departing entity exits; Grouped steps update in place; Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers; Intentional composition is preserved; Kit primitives expose style hooks; Unstyled kit output; Optional styling frameworks remain optional; Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported; Default attribution is shown; Attribution exposes a styling hook; Top-left brand is opt-in; Present mode is title-focused; Browse mode is reading-focused; Mode toggle preserves position; Keyboard navigation; Touch swipe; Direct jump; Active navigation state is exposed; Controls keep their keys; Clamp at start; Clamp at end; Uniform scaling on resize; Default canvas dimensions.

- **Finding:** “Persisting entity morphs” failed for an Arrow crossing two distinct ungrouped Scene components; see [`acceptance-findings.md`](acceptance-findings.md) F-001 and [`acceptance-evidence/arrow-continuity-observation.md`](acceptance-evidence/arrow-continuity-observation.md). Grouped scene movement did interpolate.

- **Visual evidence:** wide first/dense/last are `round0-wide-first.png`, `round0-wide-dense.png`, `round0-wide-last.png`; narrow equivalents are `round0-narrow-first.png`, `round0-narrow-dense.png`, `round0-narrow-last.png`. Project-helper captures are also present under `round0-desktop-1280-*` and `round0-helper-narrow-*`. They show readable canvas, title, captions, navigation, and attribution without visible collisions at 1280×720 and 390×844. All inspected sample steps generated zero helper warnings.

Scratch standalone and partial-monorepo projects were scaffolded and built; an existing partial Vite app was preserved and wired in scratch. Created and modified presentations were rendered, routes enumerated, builds and targeted browser verification passed. Existing presentation source hashes remained unchanged when a selected sibling was modified. See scratch `standalone`, `monorepo`, `partial-vite`, and `app` projects; screenshots `round0-modified-first.png` and `round0-modified-second.png` visibly show “First beat, revised” and the following “Second beat”.

- **Exercised through scratch skill-procedure/CLI results:** Empty or fully unscaffolded directory; Already scaffolded; Partial scaffold; Scaffold does not impose a style system; Templates resolve from skill directory; Monorepo target; Standalone project target; Non-empty project missing scaffolding; New presentation is self-contained and routed; Presentation owns its visual style; Existing presentations are preserved; Scoped modification; Checks run before done; Failures are fixed, not reported as success; Builds clean; Renders without errors; Captions and navigation present; Visual composition is inspected; Screenshot helper is project-local; Visual warnings are reviewed; Active chrome and attribution are styled locally.

- **Target unspecified or ambiguous:** Exercise covered the scratch repository's concrete target detection and no-confirm safety: a partial monorepo selected `presentations/`; bootstrap without `--confirm` wrote nothing, and explicit confirmation created the nested app. The skill's separate interactive clarification branch for a genuinely ambiguous target was not run as an independent agent/user conversation (see limitation).

- **Not independently exercised as live prompt/response conversations (limitation):** Prompt is missing details; User proceeds with partial detail; Prompt already complete; ASCII mockup for a complex step. This repository delivers instructions in a skill rather than a callable interview service. The acceptance environment provided no separate skill-runner/user dialogue; simulating internal prompts would not exercise the product boundary. Related downstream create/modify workflow and generated artifacts were exercised with scratch inputs.

All 13 named scenarios were triggered with scratch projects and browser runs. Good path: `npm run build`, `npm run verify -- --slug seeded-two`, sample verification of all nine steps, and `npm run inspect` (9 wide steps plus 9 narrow; zero warnings). Injected build, missing-sample, outline-mismatch, console-error, and stalled-transition fixtures each failed with attribution to the relevant stage; restoring the console fixture passed. Preview used `127.0.0.1`. Screenshot timing was checked against visual stability; helper default settle was 1600ms. Controlled diagnostic variants found text-bearing control/padding overlap, parent-child text collision, indistinct active progress, and absent attribution; repaired variant had no warnings and intentional overlap was marked.

- **Exercised:** Build must succeed; Sample exists and matches the outline; Missing sample fails; Every step renders cleanly; Preview uses IPv4 loopback; Console or page error fails verification; Step error fails verification; Clear outcome; Capture step screenshots; Screenshots are settled; Suspicious overlap is reported; Intentional overlap can be marked; Indistinct active chrome is reported; Unpolished attribution is reported.

- **Failure evidence:** scratch logs `fault-build` (`TS2307`); `fault-sample-missing`; `fault-sample-mismatch`; `fault-console`; `fault-stall`; successful repaired `console` fixture. Controlled diagnostic output is `scratch/acceptance-test/diagnostic-variants.log`. These were intentional injected product faults, not environment failures.

Budget: **6 steps**, set before testing in `exploration-plan.md`, one per distinct moved seam: (1) scaffold target/anchor process boundary; (2) generated create/modify workflow and identity/preservation; (3) real Motion continuity across grouped and ordinary Scene boundaries; (4) screenshot timing and diagnostics collection; (5) wide/narrow visual composition; (6) verification failure attribution and cleanup. The six steps were completed; this list is not a cap on the floor.

1. **Scaffold target and anchor boundary.** Prediction: blank standalone and partial monorepo targets should scaffold only at the detected project root, respect confirmation, and avoid clobbering unrelated files. Observation: standalone scaffold built; nested `presentations/` selected in the monorepo; no-confirm made no writes; confirmed scaffold preserved root files and built. Result: no finding.

2. **Create/modify identity and preservation.** Prediction: adding a route retains siblings; selecting a scoped edit changes only the target; quoted title data survives generation. Observation: route listing contained all four presentations; hashes for unselected step files were unchanged; quoted title compiled/rendered; selected modification built and verified. Result: no finding.

3. **Motion ownership across scene identity seam.** Prediction: stable entities morph in place while group behavior and scene replacement transitions remain coherent. Observation: grouped persist/move/enter/exit and sample continuing entity worked. In a separate Scene without groupKey, same-id Arrow jumped to its target path at 100ms while wrappers cross-faded. Result: F-001.

4. **Screenshot timing/diagnostic collection.** Prediction: settled screenshots represent rendered state and diagnostics report meaningful collisions/attribution. Observation: 1600ms helper settle captured all steps; expected injected collision/active-state/attribution warnings appeared, and repaired marked fixture was warning-free. Result: no finding.

5. **Wide/narrow composition.** Prediction: sample and edited route remain readable with controls/captions/attribution at 1280×720 and 390×844. Observation: representative first/dense/last screenshots at both widths were legible and unclipped in the inspected viewport. Result: no finding.

6. **Verification error attribution.** Prediction: each broken build/sample/render/transition fixture fails with the responsible stage, while a repaired fixture passes. Observation: all injected faults failed with stage-specific messages; repaired console fixture passed; preview was on IPv4 loopback. Result: no finding.

- The four live prompt/response cases named above were not independently exercised because the artifact is a skill instruction set and no separate agent dialogue harness was provided; synthetic scratch inputs exercised the resulting filesystem workflow. This is a product-boundary limitation, not “out of budget”.
- Did not explore publishing/export, as outside approved scope; did not fuzz layout or arbitrary malformed project structures, per the targeted-testing envelope.

- `npm test`, lint, and Validator were not run in acceptance; the acceptance skill expressly excludes automated suites, linters, and Validator. Builds and browser-backed `verify`/`inspect` commands were run only in disposable scratch projects.
- **Prior tested revision:** `a8943b4aef1e3091a02c9f16ede7a2a5922aec7a` (resolved from `acceptance-tested-revision.txt` before this pass).

ci_claims.verbatim: - **Ruling:** `npm test` runs Vitest unit and contract tests only. `npm run test:integration` runs INT-001 and INT-002. `npm run test:e2e` runs E2E-001 and E2E-002. All of these are npm scripts with no CI configuration. E2E-001 is exercised by `npm run verify`. `npm run inspect -- <slug>` runs the screenshot helper.
- **Rationale:** This follows CLAUDE.md, which forbids hosted CI, so the "every pull request" execution in the test plan means these npm scripts as the local gate.

- CI poller limitation: `codagent:wait-ci` helper returned `{"error":"no PR found for current branch"}` because its `gh pr view` query asks for unsupported JSON field `baseRefOid` (the CLI reported `Unknown JSON field: "baseRefOid"`). The repo's approved instructions and test plan explicitly say there is no hosted CI; current-head PR was inspected directly, no required checks/workflow exist, and the available PR status was CodeRabbit SUCCESS. CodeRabbit's comment states the draft PR was not reviewed. The poller failure is a tool limitation and did not imply a CI failure. No live human review was requested or triggered.

This fix round did not repeat round-0 floor coverage. It did not rerun the broad sample interaction, responsive visual pass, verification fault matrix, presentation authoring journeys, `npm test`, lint, or Validator. It did not explore other motion primitives or additional Arrow modes beyond the stable-id unidirectional Arrow across two distinct Scenes; the focused diff changed Arrow's presence context, and bidirectional rendering compiled in the existing scratch probe source but wasn't independently measured. Publishing/export and malformed-project fuzzing remain outside the approved scope. No hosted CI is configured; current PR status is recorded in the handoff.

The round-0 F-001 Arrow continuity defect is resolved at this revision. The new incoming Arrow morphs from the previous shape while distinct Scenes cross-fade. The bootstrap copy matches canonical kit code and builds/renders. **Acceptance status: READY** for the tested revision, subject to the recorded coverage limits and absent hosted CI.

The repository's approved instructions say there is no hosted CI or `.github/workflows`; npm scripts are the local validation gate. Direct current-head PR inspection showed PR #99 at the tested SHA. The only status context was CodeRabbit SUCCESS; no required automated checks were configured, and `reviewDecision` was empty. No human review was triggered. The previous round's bundled CI poller could not operate because it requested unsupported GitHub CLI field `baseRefOid`; this round used direct `gh pr view` JSON and confirmed the matching PR head/status. Hosted CI is **absent**, not passed.
